heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S handles Overture PETG natively out of the box with exceptional consistency, operating at a safe maximum print speed of 167 mm/s capped by its 14 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. Neither a hardened steel nozzle upgrade nor strict chamber preheating is required, though keeping the top glass vented during extended runs helps prevent heat creep.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with glue stick or liquid release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Max Volumetric Speed at 14.0 mm³/s in the Filament Profile to prevent extrusion starvation at standard line widths.
Set Retraction Length to 0.8 mm and Retraction Speed to 35 mm/s to eliminate fine whisker stringing common with Overture PETG.
Lower Part Cooling Fan to 20% minimum and 50% maximum, ensuring robust inter-layer bonding while avoiding excessive gloss gradients.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' set to 2 mm with a travel speed of 500 mm/s to cleanly break melt-zone surface tension without nozzle buildup.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine spiderweb artifacts across travel moves
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Overture PETG is hygroscopic and quickly absorbs atmospheric moisture, lowering melt viscosity and causing drool during non-print travels.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry filament in a dedicated dryer at 65°C for 6 hours; set OrcaSlicer Z-hop type to 'Spiral' or 'Auto' and set wipe distance to 2 mm.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Excessive bed adhesion resulting in PEI coating tearing upon part removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG chemically cross-bonds to hot PEI surfaces, creating an adhesion bond stronger than the PEI-to-steel substrate adhesive.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVP glue stick or Bambu Liquid Glue as a release interface, and let the bed cool below 35°C before removing parts.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clogs and clicking during long prints inside the closed chamber
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Heat creep softens PETG inside the cold zone above the heat break due to high internal ambient temperatures exceeding the material glass transition point.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Crack open the top glass lid or prop the front door slightly open to maintain internal chamber temperatures below 40°C.

faq.question: Do I need to leave the Bambu Lab P1S front door or glass lid open for Overture PETG?
faq.answer: Yes, it is recommended to vent the top glass or crack the door open during prolonged prints, as chamber temperatures above 45°C can cause premature filament softening and heat creep in the extruder.

faq.question: Can I print Overture PETG on the stock stainless steel nozzle of the P1S?
faq.answer: Yes, Overture PETG is non-abrasive and works safely with the stock 0.4mm stainless steel nozzle without causing accelerated bore wear.

faq.question: Why is my maximum print speed limited to 167 mm/s on the P1S?
faq.answer: At a standard 0.42 mm line width and 0.20 mm layer height, 167 mm/s equals roughly 14.0 mm³/s, which is the reliable volumetric melt capacity of the stock hotend for this viscous PETG resin.

faq.question: Should I use the Bambu Engineering Plate or Textured PEI Plate?
faq.answer: The Textured PEI Plate is optimal because the micro-texture facilitates release, though applying a light layer of glue stick is still strongly advised as a sacrificial release barrier.
